rules.boundary: Allow unpublished experience proposals only with canonical current-task provenance. Preserve signed capability decisions, mandatory approval floors and content authority.
Allow passive browser state, navigation keys, and syntactically public HTTP(S) navigation; require approval for DOM mutation until provider-attested target semantics and redirect enforcement exist.

Allow passive observation and non-committing navigation such as cursor movement, scrolling, and paging; require approval for clicks, keyboard input, drag, value changes, application lifecycle, and capture lifecycle.

Resolve the physical file target through the provisioned local resource authority. Allow current-task non-delete writes to authorized resources, including absolute paths and other registered workspaces; require approval for protected resources, missing authority and deletions. A policy approval never grants new filesystem access.

Trusted current-task terminal commands run natively with existing local software and normal project dependencies. Preserve existing sensitive-operation approvals, hard denials, pending interactions and task cancellation.

In Trusted mode, require approval for unconfined interactive terminal sessions/input and project diagnostic programs. Ctrl-C may stop an operation. A command-looking string or an Enter key does not prove read-only effects. Full-access and immutable legacy modes retain their existing policy semantics.
